summary: Ghulam Yazdani was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Indology. Educated at Aligarh Muslim University under Mohammad Ishaq and Nazir Ahmad, he held professorships at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Government College Lahore before directing archaeology for Hyderabad State (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Rome under Raniero Gnoli, and began teaching at "L'Orientale" around 1992.
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. After studying at Kyoto University (~1911–1914), he served there as a lecturer and associate professor (1934–1948), and later held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga, earning a doctorate in 1953, and served as a professor at Kyoto University (1968–1972) and Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998) studying under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, among others, and taught at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997).
Gilbert Kenneth Jenkins was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist. He was educated at Bloxham School and held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Madeleine Biardeau. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at CNRS and a member of the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences.
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2008) under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin.

Giovanni Gentile was an Italian philosopher who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the University of Pisa. He held professorships at Palermo, Pisa, and Rome (1917–1944), and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East.

Giovanni Vacca was a sinologist and historian who completed a doctorate at the University of Genoa and studied at Florence. He lectured at the University of Florence before serving at the University of Rome from 1911 to 1948.

Giovanni Verardi is a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities, he held posts at Venice, Bologna, Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993), and visiting professorships at Kyoto and Seijo universities.

Girindrasekhar Bose was an Indian psychoanalyst and philosopher who studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He was Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and founded the Indian Psychoanalytic Society.

Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster and was attested as a research fellow at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute in 2013.

Gisela Freund was an archaeologist who studied at the German University of Prague (~1941–1944). She served as Head of the Department of Prehistory at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from ~1969 to 1987.

Gisho Nakano was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and earned a doctorate from Kyushu. He was a professor and president at Koyasan University and held posts at Peking University and Tianjin Japanese Library.
Giuliana Martini is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2010, she held posts at Kyoto University and the Italian School of East Asian Studies.

Giuseppe Bardelli was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer of Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa from ~1845 to 1865.
Giuseppe Mezzofanti studied at the University of Bologna from ~1786 to 1797 and held an academic post there between ~1797 and 1831.
